I can help you with that! We want to find the missing numerator in two-thirds equals something over six. 

First, look at the denominators at the bottom: 3 and 6. How do we get from 3 to 6 using multiplication?
is 4/6. you multiply bottom by two, so you multiply top two by two also. next: 2/9 + 4/9?

You got the first one spot on! 

Now, let us look at adding two-ninths and four-ninths. Notice that both fractions already have the exact same denominator at the bottom. 

When the denominators are the same, what do we do with the numerators at the top?
I think 6/18. I am not sure.

That is a very common guess, but remember what we just talked about with the bottom numbers! When we add fractions with the same denominator, that bottom denominator stays the exact same. 

So if our denominators are both 9, what should the denominator of our answer be?
It is 9. Bottom stay same. So 2/9 + 4/9 is 6/9 because we add 2 and 4. next: 1/4 + 1/8?

Spot on, 6/9 is correct! 

Now for one-fourth plus one-eighth. This time, the denominators are 4 and 8, which are different. Remember how we turned two-thirds into four-sixths by multiplying? 

Can you change one-fourth so it has a denominator of 8?
i think answer is 2/12. i not good at this.

You are doing great, so do not worry! 

Remember, to make the denominator 8, we look at the 4. What do we multiply 4 by to get 8?
